item.title: Multichannel Lockin v3.6.2.82
item.description:
Product: Multichannel Lockin v3.6.2.82
Company: LevyLab
Release Date: Wed, 23 Sep 2026 12:58:51 -0400
Packager: Patrick Irvin

Description: Multichannel Lockin for National Instruments' Dynamic Signal Acquisition hardware (4431, 4461, 4462).
- This version is configured to handle multiple cards for simultaneous, synchronized AI/AO.
- The analog outputs can be configured to output sine, square, sawtooth, or triangle functions with (swept) DC offsets.
- Each of the analog inputs can be demodulated at multiple frequencies.

Release Notes: # Multichannel Lockin 3.6.2

## Fixes

- **#167** 3.6.1 could not start acquisition: every start failed with DAQmx error -200547. The AO output buffer is now set to two blocks before the first write, so the two-block lead introduced in 3.6.1 works as intended. Do not use 3.6.1.81.
- DAQmx read and write timeouts cut from 10 s to 5 s, so a stalled acquisition is detected and recovered sooner

No API or wire-protocol changes.

## Known issues

- Sweeps started from Transport 2.5.1.55 and earlier run with default settings: they send the old sweep field names, which this version ignores. Rebuild Transport against this package to fix.

## Testing

- Confirmed on hardware: the AO buffer is two blocks (20480 samples per task) and the tasks start without error.
- Because 3.6.1 never acquired, its changes (#160 underflow rate and reference pairing, #165 output gain) have still not run on hardware.

item.title: Multichannel Lockin v3.6.1.81
item.description:
Product: Multichannel Lockin v3.6.1.81
Company: LevyLab
Release Date: Wed, 23 Sep 2026 07:35:08 -0400
Packager: Patrick Irvin

Description: Multichannel Lockin for National Instruments' Dynamic Signal Acquisition hardware (4431, 4461, 4462).
- This version is configured to handle multiple cards for simultaneous, synchronized AI/AO.
- The analog outputs can be configured to output sine, square, sawtooth, or triangle functions with (swept) DC offsets.
- Each of the analog inputs can be demodulated at multiple frequencies.

Release Notes: # Multichannel Lockin 3.6.1

## Fixes

- **#165** Channels with a non-unity output gain now report and drive the amplitude and offset you set. Offset was not gain-compensated at all before.
- **#165** Sweep setpoints are gain-compensated too: a 0 to 1 V sweep on a gain-10 channel no longer reads back as 0 to 0.1 V.
- **#160** AO buffer underflows (-200621) should now be rare. The lock-in keeps two AO blocks ahead of the hardware instead of one, so ordinary Windows jitter no longer starves the output.
- **#160** A sweep that hits an underflow no longer steps at the recovery point: the block that failed to write is replayed instead of skipped.
- **#160** The first data point after a start or a recovery was demodulated against the wrong reference waveform. Visible only during a frequency sweep.

No API or wire-protocol changes.

## Known issues

- Sweeps started from Transport 2.5.1.55 and earlier run with default settings: they send the old sweep field names, which this version ignores. Rebuild Transport against this package to fix.

## Testing

- Automatic recovery was confirmed on hardware: 27 underflows, 26 recoveries, no manual restarts.
- The lower underflow rate, the reference fix and the #165 gain fixes have not yet run on hardware.

item.title: Multichannel Lockin v3.6.0.80
item.description:
Product: Multichannel Lockin v3.6.0.80
Company: LevyLab
Release Date: Tue, 22 Sep 2026 09:30:53 -0400
Packager: Patrick Irvin

Description: Multichannel Lockin for National Instruments' Dynamic Signal Acquisition hardware (4431, 4461, 4462).
- This version is configured to handle multiple cards for simultaneous, synchronized AI/AO.
- The analog outputs can be configured to output sine, square, sawtooth, or triangle functions with (swept) DC offsets.
- Each of the analog inputs can be demodulated at multiple frequencies.

Release Notes: # Multichannel Lockin 3.6.0 (pre-release)

## Fixes

- **#160** The lock-in no longer stops and sits in idle after an AO buffer underflow (-200621) or another recoverable DAQmx error, including mid-sweep. It now tears down and restarts its tasks on its own. Sporadic faults always recover; it gives up only after 3 attempts within 10 s of each other. The UI and API keep showing the running state during a recovery. The error log records **5160** for each successful recovery and **5161** if it gives up.
- Fixed errors -200488 / -200486 at start in `DAQmx.Clip AO Waveforms.vi`.
- Removed a broken automatic restart in Instrument.DAQ that discarded sweep data instead of restarting.

## Breaking changes

- **#164** Sweep configuration fields renamed to match the Transport Server: `Sweep Time (s)` -> `sweepTime`, `Initial Wait (s)` -> `initialWaitTime`, `Return to Start` -> `returnToStart`, `Channels` -> `sweepChannels`. These are JSON keys on the wire. **Requires Transport 1.5.2 or later.** Older Transport versions send keys this version ignores, and sweeps then run with default settings.
- Waveform attribute VIs (`Get/Set Waveform AI Channel`, `AO Channel`, `Reference Channel`, `Quadrature`, `Sweep Status`) moved into the new `Waveform.Attributes.lvlib`. Code that calls them from their old location in the Generator must be relinked.

## Changes

- Generator reworked into a proper SMO and separated from Instrument.DAQ.
- Removed obsolete gain-change behaviour; AO gain scaling now happens only in Instrument.DAQ.
- Removed dead code, including unreachable sweep states in Instrument.DAQ.

## Experimental

- **#5 External reference (PLL / FLL)** Prototype code for locking the reference to an external signal is included but switched off, and is not exposed in the UI or API. See `documentation/issue-5-external-reference.md`.

## Testing

- The #160 recovery has been verified by code review and has not yet run on hardware.
